historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of revenue_5yr_cagr and fcf_5yr_cagr (continuing-ops revenue now sourced directly from BALL_Metrics.csv, correctly restated ex-Ball-Aerospace from FY2022 onward per SEC XBRL comparative-period restatement); equity CAGR is distorted upward by the FY2024 one-off $3.6B discontinued-ops gain temporarily inflating shareholders' equity, so it is not used as the primary anchor here despite the usual house preference for it
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (9.1%) and 3yr CAGR (15.4%) diverge sharply from revenue and FCF CAGRs because FY2024 equity was inflated by the one-off $3.6B aerospace-sale gain flowing through retained earnings before ~$3B was returned via buybacks/debt paydown in FY2024-2025; equity CAGR is not a clean growth proxy for this ticker across the divestiture boundary. Revenue CAGRs are also low/negative over 3-5yr (FY2022 $13,372M was itself an unusually strong capacity-supercycle year, and FY2023-2024 saw North American capacity friction and Millersburg start-up costs), which is why the forward base-case growth path in assumptions.base starts above the trailing CAGR -- anchored instead to the current TTM run-rate (H1-2026 revenue +18% YoY) and the Millersburg capacity-relief narrative, not a mechanical extrapolation of 2022-2025 history. EPS CAGRs are not computed because reported EPS includes the FY2024 discontinued-ops gain and is not comparable across periods without a continuing-ops EPS series.

scenario_narratives.base: Structural substrate-shift volume growth (aluminum taking share from plastic/glass) continues at a moderating mid-single-digit pace as Millersburg relieves capacity constraints through 2027; margins recover from the current start-up-cost trough toward Ball's own mid-cycle target as North American operational friction eases, while thin, largely pass-through aluminum economics cap outright margin expansion.
scenario_narratives.bull: Capacity discipline across the top-3 global players (Ball, Crown, Ardagh) supports rational industry pricing, South America's outsized regional strength (+64% YoY operating earnings in Q2 2026) proves durable rather than a one-off comp, and the Millersburg ramp unlocks volume and margin upside beyond guidance as premium/specialty can mix improves blended economics.
scenario_narratives.bear: North American capacity friction and customer concentration limit pricing power through a demand downturn, regional overcapacity elsewhere in the global industry compresses returns, and elevated net debt combined with slower deleveraging under higher-for-longer rates constrains the capital-return program guided at ~$800M/year.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ball is a mature, capital-intensive, pass-through-economics aluminum can manufacturer, now a pure-play following the 2024 Ball Aerospace divestiture to BAE Systems. The valuation is built on continuing-operations (packaging-only) financials from BALL_Metrics.csv, which correctly carries FY2022-2023 restated ex-aerospace and FY2024-2025 as clean continuing-ops prints. Value here is driven by moderate structural volume growth (the plastic/glass-to-aluminum substrate shift), a margin recovery from the current Millersburg start-up-cost trough toward Ball's own mid-cycle target, and capital returned via buybacks that fund a flat share count against fully-expensed SBC. The business is not a growth compounder -- it is a scaled, disciplined industrial with real balance-sheet leverage, which the 15x terminal cap multiple and 8% WACC reflect versus the 20x/lower-WACC treatment appropriate for a software business.
key_risks_to_valuation: North American capacity friction and Millersburg start-up costs (~$35M in 2026) could persist longer than guided, delaying the margin recovery baked into the base case
Customer concentration among large global beverage companies limits pricing power against aluminum/energy cost inflation despite contractual pass-through provisions
Elevated net debt (~$6.7B, ~3.3-3.5x EBITDA) constrains capital-return flexibility if a downturn coincides with higher-for-longer rates
EMEA and South America currency translation exposure can obscure underlying operating performance in reported (as opposed to constant-currency) results

Trailing revenue CAGRs are low/slightly negative (3yr -0.5%, 5yr 2.2%) because FY2022 was an unusually strong capacity-supercycle year -- the base case's forward growth path is anchored to the current TTM run-rate and Millersburg capacity relief rather than trailing history, which is a judgment call worth revisiting if the current volume acceleration proves temporary

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 44.83-68.29
data_sources.financials: research/BALL/Reports/BALL_Metrics.csv and BALL.duckdb core_metrics for revenue, balance-sheet, share-count, SBC and buyback anchors (revenue populated FY2018-2025 following the XBRL parser fallback fix in commit 35a86bba); cross-checked against SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000009389) to confirm the FY2022/FY2023 continuing-operations restatement (ex-Ball-Aerospace) embedded in the CSV
data_sources.qualitative: research/BALL/Reports/BALL_Analysis.json (2026-09-26), including Q2 2026 earnings commentary, FY2026 guidance, and bull/bear case points

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK0000009389 / BALL_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column, TTM ended 2026-06-30 = FY2025 (28) + H1-2026 (13) - H1-2025 (18) = 23; no separate equity-award-tax-withholding line disclosed distinct from the buyback line, so the cash-flow SBC add-back is used as-is
inputs.wacc_rationale: US industrial manufacturer, moderate leverage (~net debt/EBITDA ~3.3x post-aerospace-sale deleveraging). Risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST, Sep-2026), ERP ~5%, unlevered beta ~0.9 for packaging manufacturing re-levered at BALL's capital structure, plus a small size/cyclicality premium. WACC = 8.0%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Finance leases are $7M (Q2 2026, XBRL FinanceLeaseLiability) -- immaterial (<0.1% of net debt) and left out of both flows and net debt; operating lease liability not separately disclosed as a distinct XBRL tag for BALL and is not material to a company that owns its ~70 manufacturing plants. No lease adjustment made.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is $20M (Q2 2026, XBRL MinorityInterest) against $5.77B of total equity -- immaterial (<0.4%). Reported net income and FCF are used as-is (essentially all attributable to Ball shareholders); no NCI deduction applied.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF component route (standard operating-company manufacturer, routed via dcf-methods/SKILL.md; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco). Ball divested Ball Aerospace to BAE Systems (closed Feb-2024); BALL_Metrics.csv/core_metrics revenue is now populated FY2018-2025 (parser gap fixed in commit 35a86bba, which added RevenueFromContractWithCustomerIncludingAssessedTax as an XBRL revenue fallback) and carries FY2022 (13,372) and FY2023 (12,062) already restated to continuing operations ex-Ball-Aerospace (confirmed against SEC XBRL comparative-period restatements: FY2022 was originally filed at 15,349 including ~1,977 of aerospace revenue, later restated to 13,372 in the FY2024 10-K comparative column once aerospace was reclassified to discontinued operations; FY2023 likewise restated from 14,029 to 12,062). FY2024 (11,795) and FY2025 (13,161) are clean continuing-ops (pure-play packaging) prints. base_revenue is TTM ended 2026-06-30 = FY2025 (13,161) + H1-2026 (7,600) - H1-2025 (6,435) = $14,326M, verified directly against the corrected BALL_Metrics.csv (exact match), reflecting the current volume-growth + aluminum-cost-pass-through run rate (H1-2026 revenue +18.1% YoY, consistent with Analysis JSON Q1/Q2 commentary). Net income for FY2024 in the CSV ($4,014M) is dominated by a $3,584M discontinued-operations gain on the aerospace sale and is NOT used as a margin anchor -- continuing-operations EBITDA/EBIT margin history (FY2023 ~16.6%, FY2024 ~12.5% [Millersburg start-up cost drag], FY2025 ~15.7%) lands on an FY0 EBITDA margin of ~15.5%, consistent with a pass-through-economics can manufacturer per the Analysis JSON. Net debt taken from Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet (total debt 7,220 - cash 491 = 6,729), shares outstanding 267.139M diluted weighted average Q2 2026 (XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding), both matching BALL_Metrics.csv/core_metrics exactly. SBC is very low (~0.2% of revenue) as is typical for a capital-intensive industrial manufacturer versus a tech/SaaS name -- share count held flat per house convention since SBC is fully expensed in the flows; BALL is also a heavy repurchaser ($1,321M FY2025 buybacks) funding that flat count with real cash, so the flat-share assumption is well-supported by actual capital allocation, not just a modelling convention. last_fcf/reported_fcf/sbc are TTM ended 2026-06-30 (FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025), matching the TTM revenue base for internal consistency: reported_fcf $827M, owner FCF (less TTM SBC of $23M) $804M. Note BALL is seasonally FCF-negative in H1 (working-capital build ahead of peak summer can demand) and FY2026 guidance is for full-year FCF "above $900 million"; the TTM figure of $827M sits below that guided full-year number because it still carries a weak H1-2026 print -- the component build in assumptions.base ramps off the TTM base rather than assuming the guided $900M+ is already banked.

bear.narrative: North American capacity friction and Millersburg start-up costs (~$35M in 2026) persist longer than guided, and regional overcapacity elsewhere (a real industry risk the Analysis JSON flags) compresses can pricing even as Ball itself holds capacity discipline. Customer concentration among a handful of large global beverage companies limits the ability to pass through cost inflation or hold price in a downturn. Consumer demand softens (destocking cycle, weak discretionary spending on premium/RTD formats), aluminum and energy cost volatility pressures margins faster than contractual pass-throughs can catch up, and elevated leverage (~$6.7B net debt) combined with higher-for-longer rates raises financing costs on growth capex, slowing the deleveraging trajectory.

base.narrative: Millersburg fully ramps through 2027, relieving North America/EMEA capacity constraints; global volumes continue the current run of consecutive quarterly growth (~2-4%/yr structurally) as the plastic/glass-to-aluminum substrate shift continues, plus low-single-digit price/mix and aluminum cost pass-through. EBITDA margin recovers from the Millersburg start-up-cost trough (~15.5%) toward the mid-cycle ~16.5% level as start-up costs roll off and utilization normalizes. Capex settles at a normalized maintenance+modest-growth level (~3.1-3.4% of revenue) well below the 2021-22 capacity supercycle (13-14% of revenue at the time). Working capital is a modest drag on growth (negative capture) consistent with a manufacturer carrying receivables and metal inventory ahead of payables. Cash tax rate holds near the recent effective continuing-ops rate (~23-24%), with no valuation-allowance or one-off benefit to unwind.

bull.narrative: Millersburg ramp and industry-wide capacity discipline (Ball/Crown/Ardagh ~60% of global revenue) support rational pricing and faster-than-expected margin recovery. South America's ~64% YoY operating-earnings growth (Q2 2026) persists as a genuine structural regional tailwind rather than a one-off comp, specialty/premium can mix (energy, RTD cocktails, hard seltzer) continues to improve blended economics, and the substrate shift from plastic/glass accelerates as EPR/deposit-return regulation spreads. Capital allocation stays disciplined, with buybacks continuing to fund the flat share count.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 shifted to 25/50/25. Bear weight raised above house default because BALL carries real leverage (~net debt/EBITDA ~3.3-3.5x) into a business with thin, largely pass-through margins and acknowledged near-term operational friction (capacity constraints, Millersburg start-up costs) that management itself flagged by holding rather than raising FY2026 guidance despite a Q2 beat -- this is closer to margin-compression risk than going-concern risk, but is more than a generic downside case. Bull weight trimmed to match because the bull case (sustained South America strength, full capacity relief, industry-wide pricing discipline all holding simultaneously) requires several independent things to go right, similar to the house's guidance for asymmetric-upside-needed bull cases.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
